knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE,
                      fig.width=8, fig.height=5, fig.pos="H")

## Overview

The Analysis-1 elastic-net nomogram was **developed and frozen on MIMIC-IV v3.1**
(single centre, Boston). Here it is applied **without any refitting** to the
**eICU Collaborative Research Database v2.0** (200+ US ICUs) to measure how
well it *transports* to a completely independent, multi-centre population. The
eICU hour-6 landmark table (`landmark_h6_eicu.parquet`) was built by
`21_eicu_external_panel.py` using the identical cohort, panel, hourly-SOFA,
onset, and feature definitions as the MIMIC pipeline (scripts `02/03/07/08`).

We report three things a proper external validation must separate:

1. **Frozen transport**: discrimination and calibration of the MIMIC model
   applied as-is (the honest deployment scenario).
2. **Recalibration**: how much a simple intercept + slope update recovers,
   distinguishing *miscalibration* (fixable) from *loss of discrimination*
   (not).
3. **Internal eICU ceiling**: an elastic net refit on eICU itself, showing the
   best discrimination the same features can achieve in this population.

### The one cross-dataset caveat

Sepsis-3 requires a culture drawn near an antibiotic. eICU captures
microbiology for only ~1.5% of stays but antibiotics for ~83%, so requiring a
culture would make the *label* (not the model) untransportable. We therefore
trigger suspected infection on the first qualifying antibiotic order (refining
timing with a culture when one exists). This is a property of eICU's data
capture and is the primary caveat on the numbers below.

## Load Libraries and Data

```{r load}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(glmnet); library(pROC); library(PRROC)
})
set.seed(486649)

find_data <- function(f) {
  cands <- c(file.path("../../../processed_data", f),
             file.path("processed_data", f), f)
  hit <- cands[file.exists(cands)][1]
  if (is.na(hit)) stop("cannot find ", f)
  hit
}
OUT <- dirname(find_data("21_landmark_h6_eicu.parquet"))
FIG <- if (dir.exists("figure")) "figure" else { dir.create("figure"); "figure" }

ext   <- arrow::read_parquet(find_data("21_landmark_h6_eicu.parquet"))
coefs <- read.csv(find_data("10_analysis1_coefs.csv"))          # frozen MIMIC model
cat(sprintf("eICU landmark: %d at-risk stays, onset-within-12h rate %.3f (%d events)\n",
            nrow(ext), mean(ext$onset_within_h), sum(ext$onset_within_h)))
```

## Rebuild the Frozen Design Matrix

The feature design from script `10` is reconstructed exactly: vitals and
severity scores are median-imputed; labs are median-imputed with a "was-measured"
indicator (`_msg`); 6-hour slopes are zero-imputed with a `_msg` indicator; plus
age and sex. Imputation uses **eICU** central values, as appropriate when
deploying a frozen model on a new population.

```{r design}
build_design <- function(d) {
  vitals <- c("hr","resp_rate","map","spo2","temp_c","gcs")
  scores <- c("sofa_total","qsofa","sirs")
  labs   <- c("lactate","creatinine","wbc","pf_ratio")
  slopes <- c("hr_slope6","resp_rate_slope6","map_slope6","spo2_slope6")
  df <- data.frame(row.names = seq_len(nrow(d)))
  for (v in c(vitals, scores)) {
    x <- d[[v]]; x[is.na(x)] <- median(x, na.rm = TRUE); df[[v]] <- x }
  for (v in labs) {
    x <- d[[v]]; df[[paste0(v, "_msg")]] <- as.integer(is.na(x))
    x[is.na(x)] <- median(x, na.rm = TRUE); df[[v]] <- x }
  for (v in slopes) {
    x <- d[[v]]; df[[paste0(v, "_msg")]] <- as.integer(is.na(x))
    x[is.na(x)] <- 0; df[[v]] <- x }
  df$age    <- d$age
  df$female <- as.integer(d$gender == "F")
  df
}
X  <- build_design(ext)
y  <- ext$onset_within_h
cat(sprintf("Design matrix: %d rows x %d features\n", nrow(X), ncol(X)))
```

## Score the Frozen MIMIC Model (No Refitting)

The linear predictor is assembled by name from the frozen coefficients to
prevent silent misalignment of term ordering.

```{r frozen-score}
b0 <- coefs$coef[coefs$term == "(Intercept)"]
terms <- setdiff(coefs$term, "(Intercept)")
stopifnot(all(terms %in% names(X)))                  # alignment guard
lp <- b0 + as.matrix(X[, terms]) %*% coefs$coef[match(terms, coefs$term)]
lp <- as.numeric(lp)
risk_frozen <- plogis(lp)
```

## Discrimination, Calibration, and Recalibration

AUROC measures discrimination (rank ordering, invariant to calibration).
Calibration-in-the-large compares mean predicted risk to the observed event
rate. The **calibration slope** (from `glm(y ~ lp)`) is the gold-standard
transportability summary: slope 1 = perfect, <1 = frozen risks too extreme
(typical under dataset shift), and the intercept captures baseline-rate drift.

```{r metrics}
ok <- complete.cases(y, risk_frozen)
y <- y[ok]; risk_frozen <- risk_frozen[ok]; lp <- lp[ok]
ext <- ext[ok, ]; X <- X[ok, ]

roc_frozen <- roc(y, risk_frozen, quiet = TRUE, direction = "<")
auc_ci     <- ci.auc(roc_frozen)                    # DeLong 95% CI
prauc      <- pr.curve(scores.class0 = risk_frozen[y == 1],
                       scores.class1 = risk_frozen[y == 0])$auc.integral
brier      <- mean((risk_frozen - y)^2)

recal <- glm(y ~ lp, family = binomial)
cal_intercept <- coef(recal)[1]
cal_slope     <- coef(recal)[2]
risk_recal    <- predict(recal, type = "response")
brier_recal   <- mean((risk_recal - y)^2)

cil_pred <- mean(risk_frozen); cil_obs <- mean(y)

summary_tbl <- data.frame(
  metric = c("N (at-risk stays)", "Events (onset within 12h)", "Event rate",
             "AUROC (frozen)", "AUROC 95% CI",
             "PR-AUC (frozen)", "Brier (frozen)",
             "Mean predicted risk", "Observed rate",
             "Calibration slope", "Calibration intercept",
             "Brier (after recalibration)"),
  value = c(
    nrow(ext), sum(y), sprintf("%.3f", cil_obs),
    sprintf("%.3f", as.numeric(auc(roc_frozen))),
    sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", auc_ci[1], auc_ci[3]),
    sprintf("%.3f", prauc), sprintf("%.4f", brier),
    sprintf("%.3f", cil_pred), sprintf("%.3f", cil_obs),
    sprintf("%.3f", cal_slope), sprintf("%.3f", cal_intercept),
    sprintf("%.4f", brier_recal)))
knitr::kable(summary_tbl, caption = "Frozen-model external validation on eICU.")
```

## Internal eICU Ceiling (Elastic Net Refit)

Refitting the same elastic-net design on eICU with 5-fold out-of-sample
prediction separates loss of discrimination from miscalibration. If the refit
AUROC is close to the frozen AUROC, discrimination transports and any gap
to MIMIC's 0.775 reflects population difficulty, not model failure.

```{r internal-ceiling}
Xm <- as.matrix(X)
folds <- sample(rep(1:5, length.out = nrow(Xm)))
oos <- numeric(nrow(Xm))
for (k in 1:5) {
  tr <- folds != k
  cvfit <- cv.glmnet(Xm[tr, ], y[tr], family = "binomial",
                     alpha = 0.5, nfolds = 5, standardize = TRUE)
  oos[!tr] <- as.numeric(predict(cvfit, Xm[!tr, ],
                                 s = "lambda.min", type = "response"))
}
roc_int <- roc(y, oos, quiet = TRUE, direction = "<")
delong_frozen_vs_int <- roc.test(roc_int, roc_frozen, method = "delong")$p.value
cat(sprintf("Internal eICU refit AUROC: %.3f  |  frozen-transport AUROC: %.3f\n",
            as.numeric(auc(roc_int)), as.numeric(auc(roc_frozen))))
cat(sprintf("DeLong p (internal vs frozen): %.3g\n", delong_frozen_vs_int))
```

## Save Results

```{r save}
res <- data.frame(
  auroc_frozen   = as.numeric(auc(roc_frozen)),
  auroc_lo       = auc_ci[1], auroc_hi = auc_ci[3],
  prauc_frozen   = prauc,
  brier_frozen   = brier,
  brier_recal    = brier_recal,
  cal_slope      = cal_slope,
  cal_intercept  = cal_intercept,
  mean_pred      = cil_pred,
  obs_rate       = cil_obs,
  auroc_internal = as.numeric(auc(roc_int)),
  delong_p_internal_vs_frozen = delong_frozen_vs_int,
  n_stays        = nrow(ext),
  n_events       = sum(y))
res[] <- lapply(res, function(x) if (is.numeric(x)) round(x, 4) else x)
write.csv(res, file.path(OUT, "22_external_validation_eicu.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(t(res), caption = "eICU external-validation summary (saved to CSV).")
```

## Calibration Curve

Decile-binned observed vs predicted risk, for the frozen model and after
intercept/slope recalibration.

```{r calibration, fig.width=6, fig.height=6}
png(file.path(FIG, "22_calibration_eicu.png"), width = 1100, height = 1000, res = 200)
decile_cal <- function(p) {
  bins <- cut(p, quantile(p, seq(0, 1, 0.1)), include.lowest = TRUE)
  aggregate(cbind(pred = p, obs = y), list(bin = bins), mean)
}
cf <- decile_cal(risk_frozen); cr <- decile_cal(risk_recal)
rng <- range(0, cf$pred, cf$obs, cr$pred, cr$obs)
plot(cf$pred, cf$obs, pch = 19, col = "firebrick", xlim = rng, ylim = rng,
     xlab = "Predicted risk", ylab = "Observed onset rate",
     main = "eICU calibration (deciles)")
lines(cf$pred, cf$obs, col = "firebrick")
points(cr$pred, cr$obs, pch = 17, col = "steelblue")
lines(cr$pred, cr$obs, col = "steelblue")
abline(0, 1, lty = 2, col = "grey50")
legend("topleft", c("Frozen MIMIC model", "After recalibration", "Ideal"),
       pch = c(19, 17, NA), lty = c(1, 1, 2),
       col = c("firebrick", "steelblue", "grey50"), bty = "n", cex = 0.8)
dev.off()
```

```{r show-fig, echo=FALSE, out.width="70%", fig.align="center", fig.cap="eICU calibration: frozen MIMIC model versus intercept/slope recalibration."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(FIG, "22_calibration_eicu.png"))
```

## Interpretation

The frozen MIMIC nomogram's **discrimination transports** to eICU if the
frozen-transport AUROC sits near the internal-refit ceiling and the DeLong test
finds no meaningful gap. **Calibration** is read from the slope and intercept:
a slope below 1 means the MIMIC-trained risks are too extreme for eICU (the
usual consequence of case-mix and measurement-practice shift across 200+
hospitals) and is corrected by the one-line recalibration whose improved Brier
is reported above. The persisting cross-dataset caveat is the antibiotic-based
suspicion trigger; the discrimination result is nonetheless a genuine, fully
out-of-sample test of the model on an independent multi-centre population,
closing the project's one remaining open item.
```
